lead: Audio and video are large streams of samples and frames. Compression makes them small enough to store and send. Audio compression removes what the ear will not notice, using masking. Video compression removes what the eye will not notice and also predicts each frame from earlier frames. Motion compensation is the prediction step: the coder finds where a block moved and sends only the difference. Phone calls, music streaming, video calls and OTT video use these ideas.
prereq: You need: Chapter 4.6 for lossy compression and Chapter 4.2 for audio samples and video frames.

blocks.text: PCM is the baseline for digital audio. A microphone signal is sampled at a fixed rate, and each sample is stored with a fixed number of bits. A mono CD signal uses 44 100 samples per second and 16 bits per sample, so one second needs 705 600 bits, or 88.2 kB. PCM keeps every sample. Lossy audio compression sends fewer bits by removing parts the ear cannot hear well.

The ear behaves like a frequency analyser. A loud tone raises the hearing threshold near its frequency. A quiet tone close in frequency becomes inaudible. This is frequency masking. A loud sound also hides a quiet sound just before and just after it. This is temporal masking. A psychoacoustic model estimates these masked regions from the signal.

The coder splits the signal into short overlapping blocks and applies the modified discrete cosine transform (MDCT). The MDCT turns each block into frequency coefficients. Coefficients inside masked regions get coarse quantization or zero bits. Coefficients outside masked regions get fine quantization. MP3 and AAC use this scheme.
Speech codecs often use a different model. They predict the vocal tract with a linear filter and send the filter parameters plus a small residual. This works at low bit rates for speech.

blocks.where: R is the bit rate in bits per second; f<sub>s</sub> is the sample rate in samples per second; b is the bits per sample; C is the number of channels.

blocks.text: A video is a sequence of frames. An I-frame (intra frame) is coded from itself only, like a still image. A P-frame (predicted frame) is coded from an earlier reference frame. A B-frame (bidirectional frame) may use an earlier and a later reference frame. A group of pictures (GOP) is the repeating pattern from one I-frame to the next I-frame.

For a P-frame, the coder splits the current frame into blocks, often 16×16 macroblocks, which are blocks of pixels. For each block it searches the reference frame for a similar block. The search is motion estimation. The displacement from the current block to the matched block is the motion vector. If the matched block starts at (x+5, y−3) when the current block starts at (x, y), the motion vector is (5, −3). It is a displacement, not a position.

Motion compensation uses that vector to copy the matched block as a prediction. The coder subtracts the prediction from the current block. The difference is the residual. If the match is good, the residual has little energy and few nonzero values. The coder sends the motion vector and the coded residual. The decoder copies the same prediction and adds the residual back. Some syllabi call motion compensation motion-compensated prediction.
B-frames need two reference frames, so they need more memory and introduce delay. A GOP balances random access, compression and delay.

sections.h3: Coding the residual to a bitstream

blocks.text: The residual block goes through a two-dimensional discrete cosine transform (DCT). The DCT turns the block into coefficients: one low-frequency term and many higher-frequency terms. Natural images have most energy in low frequencies, so many high-frequency coefficients are small. Quantization divides each coefficient by a step size and rounds to an integer. A larger step gives more zeros and fewer bits, but more error. The quantized coefficients are scanned in an order that puts low frequencies first, then run-length coded and entropy coded. Entropy coding assigns short codes to common symbols.

The decoder reverses the steps. It entropy-decodes the coefficients, dequantizes them, applies the inverse DCT to get the residual, and adds the motion-compensated prediction. It stores the rebuilt frame as the reference for later frames.

The figure shows the encoder path. Motion estimation uses the current frame and the reference frame. Motion compensation forms the residual. DCT and quantization reduce it to coefficients. Entropy coding writes the bitstream. The motion vector is also sent, because the decoder needs it to rebuild the prediction.

figure.caption: The 16 × 16 block at (x, y) finds its best match at (x+5, y−3) in the reference frame, so the motion vector is (5, −3). Sending 16 bits of vector and 240 bits of residual, 256 bits in all, replaces 2048 raw bits: 8 : 1.

spec.aria: A pixel grid of the reference frame with the dashed current 16 by 16 block and the shaded matching block 5 pixels right and 3 up, joined by the vector (5, −3); beside it the bit counts and two bars, raw 2048 bits against coded 256 bits.

examples.question: A 16×16 macroblock in the current frame starts at (x, y). It matches a block starting at (x+5, y−3) in the reference frame. Each pixel uses 8 bits. Each motion-vector component uses 8 bits. After motion compensation the residual has 40 nonzero coefficients, and each coefficient is coded with 6 bits. Ignore headers. (a) Write the motion vector. (b) Find the bits and bytes for the coded block. (c) Compare with the raw block and give the ratio.
steps: The matched block starts 5 columns to the right and 3 rows in the negative direction from the current block. Motion vector = (5, −3).
Vector bits = 8 bits for x + 8 bits for y = 16 bits.
Residual bits = 40 nonzero coefficients × 6 bits = 240 bits.
Total coded bits = 16 + 240 = 256 bits. Total coded bytes = 256 ÷ 8 = 32 B.
Raw block = 16 × 16 = 256 pixels. Raw bits = 256 × 8 = 2048 bits = 256 B.
Ratio = raw bits ÷ coded bits = 2048 ÷ 256 = 8, so 8:1.
examples.answer: The motion vector is (5, −3); the block needs 256 bits = 32 B, an 8:1 reduction from the 2048-bit raw block.
examples.check:
mx = 5
my = -3
vbits = 8 + 8
rcoeff = 40
cbits = 6
rbits = rcoeff * cbits
total_bits = vbits + rbits
total_bytes = total_bits // 8
pixels = 16 * 16
raw_bits = pixels * 8
raw_bytes = raw_bits // 8
ratio = raw_bits // total_bits
for v in [mx, my, vbits, rbits, total_bits, total_bytes, raw_bits, raw_bytes, ratio]:
    print(v)

traps: A motion vector is a displacement, not the absolute position of the matched block. (5, −3) means five columns right and three rows in the negative direction from the current block.
An I-frame does not use motion compensation. Do not add motion-vector bits to an I-frame.
Quantization is the main lossy step. The DCT and entropy coding are reversible; do not blame them for the lost detail.
A B-frame can use a later reference frame, so its decoding order may differ from its display order.
Masking is statistical for a population, not a promise for every listener. A coefficient marked masked may still be sent when bits are available.

quiz.q: What does PCM store for each audio sample?
quiz.a: A fixed number of bits, at a fixed sample rate.

quiz.q: Why does a loud tone make a nearby quiet tone easier to compress?
quiz.a: The loud tone raises the hearing threshold near its frequency, so the quiet tone is masked and can use coarse quantization or zero bits.

quiz.q: A 16×16 block at (x, y) matches a block at (x−4, y+7). Write the motion vector.
quiz.a: (−4, 7): four columns left and seven rows in the positive direction from the current block.

quiz.q: Why does a P-frame send a residual as well as a motion vector?
quiz.a: The matched block is only a prediction. The residual corrects the difference between the prediction and the current block, so the decoder can rebuild the exact block within quantization error.

quiz.q: A motion vector uses 6 bits per component. The residual has 25 nonzero coefficients at 5 bits each. Find the total bits for the block, ignoring headers.
quiz.a: Vector bits = 6+6=12. Residual bits =25×5=125. Total =12+125=137 bits.

quiz.q: What is a GOP and why does it contain I-frames?
quiz.a: A group of pictures is the repeating frame pattern from one I-frame to the next. I-frames allow random access and reset prediction errors.

quiz.q: Why can a larger quantization step reduce bit rate but increase visible error?
quiz.a: A larger step rounds more coefficients to zero or to nearby values, so fewer bits are sent. The same rounding adds error to the rebuilt block.
A loud sound hides a quiet sound just before and just after it in time.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern video codecs such as AV1 and VVC refine the same loop: more block shapes, better motion search and better entropy coding. Audio codecs add better psychoacoustic models and low-delay modes for calls. Rate-distortion optimization chooses motion vectors and quantizers by balancing bits and error. Search for 'perceptual audio coding', 'block matching motion estimation' and 'rate-distortion optimization' to go deeper.
